title: 1993 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: When \(10^{93} - 93\) is expressed as a single whole number, the sum of the digits is

solutions.text:
Subtracting \(93\) from \(10^{93}\) (a \(1\) followed by \(93\) zeros) gives a number that is \(91\) nines followed by \(07.\)

The digit sum is \(91 \times 9 + 0 + 7 = 819 + 7 = 826.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: \(10^{93}\) is a \(1\) followed by \(93\) zeros; subtracting \(93\) changes only the right end
The result is a block of nines ending in \(07;\) determine how many nines there are
